    "operation": "etymology",
    "chain": "Fyre < Middle English fyr < Old English fȳr; cognate with Old High German fiur, Greek pyr",
    "reading": "The elemental fire, the primordial heat that transforms and purifies.",

    "source": "Oxford English Dictionary, entry 'fire'",
    "confidence": 0.95

  {

    "reading": "That which flees or is elusive—the spark that escapes the hearth.",
    "languages": ["en", "fr", "la"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.4
  },
  {
    "operation": "cross_language_homophone",
    "chain": "Fyre ~ Greek 'pyr' (fire) via sound shift p/f; also French 'fer' (iron) with y as glide",
    "reading": "Fire and iron are one—the forge where metal is born from flame.",
    "languages": ["en", "grc", "fr"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.55
  },
  {
    "operation": "anagram",
    "chain": "Fyre -> 'fry' + e; fry (cook by fire) + silent e (mystery); also 'refy' (to refine, back-formation)",
    "reading": "To fry is to be transformed by heat; the silent e is the hidden spirit.",
    "languages": ["en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.35
  },
  {
    "operation": "notariqon",
    "chain": "F-Y-R-E: F = flamma (flame), Y = ylem (primal matter), R = rota (wheel), E = essentia (essence)",
    "reading": "Flame, primal matter, wheel, essence—the cycle of creation through fire.",
    "languages": ["la", "en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.3
  },
  {
    "operation": "letter_symbol",
    "chain": "F (digamma, 6) + Y (Greek upsilon, 20) + R (Latin R, 18) + E (Greek epsilon, 5); F = hearth, Y = fork, R = head, E = breath",
    "reading": "The hearth's fork lifts the head of breath—fire as the breath of life.",
    "languages": ["en", "grc", "la"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.25
  },
  {
    "operation": "numerical",
    "chain": "F=6, Y=25 (alphabet position), R=18, E=5; sum=54; 5+4=9; 9 = completion, but also Greek theta (death/rebirth)",
    "reading": "Fire’s number is nine—the end of a cycle and the seed of renewal.",
    "languages": ["en", "grc"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.2
  },
  {
    "operation": "etymology",
    "chain": "Fyre < Old Norse 'fýri' (fire) but also 'fýr' (haste); double root: heat and speed",
    "reading": "Fire is not only heat but urgency—the swift devourer.",
    "languages": ["en", "non"],
    "source": "Cleasby-Vigfusson Old Norse Dictionary, 'fýr'",
    "confidence": 0.7
  }
]
